content.title: LinkedIn — what buyers miss on light jet value
content.hook: The cheapest light jet on the market is almost never the best buy.
content.body:
The cheapest light jet on the market is almost never the best buy.

Asking price is the number everyone looks at. It's also the number that tells you the least. What actually moves your total cost of ownership is the stuff a spec sheet buries:

— Are the engines on a program, or are you one hot section away from a six-figure surprise?
— When was the last major inspection, and how much runway is left before the next one?
— Is the avionics stack current enough to fly the airspace you actually fly?

We've watched buyers save a hundred grand on acquisition and give it all back in the first year. Position beats price. Know what you're really buying before you're asked to defend it.

content.title: LinkedIn — founder POV on representing both sides
content.hook: People ask how we can represent buyers and sellers in the same market without it being a conflict.
content.body:
People ask how we can represent buyers and sellers in the same market without it being a conflict.

Here's the honest answer: because the job isn't to win a side. It's to tell the truth about the airplane and the market, every time, to whoever we're sitting across from.

When you've valued the same tail from both directions, you stop guessing. You know what a clean logbook is worth, what a deferred inspection really costs, and where the number lands when emotion leaves the room. That's not a conflict — that's the whole edge.

Representation on every side of the deal, with the same data and the same standard. That's the firm we wanted to build.

content.title: LinkedIn — fresh maintenance is repricing the market
content.hook: Fresh maintenance is quietly repricing the used-jet market.
content.body:
Fresh maintenance is quietly repricing the used-jet market.

For years, buyers chased the lowest sticker. That's changing. With shop slots backed up and inspection costs climbing, a jet that's already had its big-ticket work done — fresh inspections, engines on a program — is trading at a real premium and selling faster.

The reason is simple: the next owner isn't buying an airplane, they're buying a position. A clean, current logbook means predictable costs and no six-figure surprise in year one.

If you're weighing two similar jets, look past the asking price to what's already been paid for. That gap is where the value hides.

content.title: LinkedIn — we tell buyers to walk away
content.hook: We tell buyers to walk away more often than they expect.
content.body:
We tell buyers to walk away more often than they expect.

It surprises people that a brokerage would talk a client out of a deal. But representing the buyer means representing the buyer — not the transaction. If the pre-buy turns up a story the logbooks don't support, or the number stops making sense, the right call is sometimes 'not this one.'

We've walked clients away from airplanes they loved. Every time, the next deal was better for it.

Trust is the only thing we actually sell. The airplane is just what's on the invoice.
